notes: Fourth draft. The applicability check also screens for NIS2, DORA, the Cyber Resilience Act and the Data Act; they are not covered by the Hub, and a positive result offers a consultation with SenecAI. Otherwise as the third draft: The classification reads the AI system record (origin, use, stage, areas of use, affected groups, capabilities) and asks only what the record cannot settle: the role is asked only for bought systems, scope only before production, the Art. 5 screen only where the capabilities show a pattern, interaction and generated content come from the record. Sector at onboarding is chosen from a list (pre-filling each system's area of use) with an optional description. Classification starts from the system's areas of use, so questions and Annex I/III options that cannot apply are not asked; the Art. 5 screen asks indirect risk questions instead of listing the prohibited practices; Art. 26(1) is not listed separately when the company is also the provider; Art. 26(7) applies only when the system affects the company's own workers; the applicability check no longer flags DORA or NIS2 and takes the sector as free text. Updated to the Digital Omnibus on AI (Reg. (EU) 2026/1744, OJ L 24.7.2026): high-risk dates 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I); machinery moved to Annex I, Section B; new Art. 4 wording; new prohibitions in Art. 5(1)(ba)–(bb) from 2 December 2026; Art. 50(2) transition to 2 December 2026; Art. 6(1a)–(1c) on safety components. Draft: needs legal review by the spec owner before it is published.
